title: Review to Tighten Licensing Conditions for Electricity Retailers to Better Protect Consumers
what_it_is: Review to Tighten Licensing Conditions for Electricity Retailers to Better Protect Consumers

sections.label: Electricity retailer licensing review
sections.summary: The Minister was asked when the review of tighter licensing conditions for electricity retailers will be completed and how higher costs will be prevented from passing to consumers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) when is the Ministry expecting to complete its review of tightening licensing conditions for electricity retailers to protect consumers; and (b) how does the Ministry ensure that higher costs will not be passed on to consumers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: These guardrails include enhancements to the regulatory requirements on electricity retailers to strengthen consumer protection and the retailers' ability to withstand market volatility.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: On 1 February 2023, EMA launched a public consultation on the proposed enhancements to the regulatory framework for electricity retailers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The consultation will close on 3 March 2023.

sections.label: Retailer hedging and performance bonds
sections.summary: EMA intends to require retailers to hedge at least 80% of retail contract quantity on a rolling 24-month forward basis and provide a performance bond.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Moving forward, EMA intends to require all retailers to hedge at least 80% of their retail contract quantity on a rolling 24-month forward basis.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Retailers would have to provide a performance bond, to cover their projected residual unhedged quantities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: This increased hedging requirements are intended to increase the resilience of retailers during periods of market volatility.

sections.label: Contracts-for-Difference and cost impact
sections.summary: Retailers can enter Contracts-for-Difference with suppliers holding physical generation assets, and MTI and EMA calibrated enhancements to keep cost impact reasonable.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Besides the electricity futures market, retailers can also enter into contract for different Contracts-for-Difference, which suppliers with physical generation assets such as generation companies, waste to energy plants or solar providers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: MTI and EMA have carefully calibrated enhancements to ensure that any cost impact is reasonable.
